'''Clara E. Walke Hall''' (October 3, 1930 – May 28, 2014) was an American research chemist at the [[National Institutes of Health]] from 1959 to 1999. Hall and geneticist [[Elizabeth F. Neufeld]]'s research on genetic conditions affecting [[Lysosome|lysosomes]] led to Neufeld receiving the [[Lasker-DeBakey Clinical Medical Research Award]] in 1982. 

== Education and career ==
[[File:Clara Hall (cropped).jpg|thumb|Hall (l) and Neufeld (r) in 1975]]
Clara E. Walke Hall was born October 3, 1930, in [[New York City]].{{sfn|Dignity Memorial|2014}} She earned a B.S. in chemistry from [[Hunter College]].{{sfn|NIH Record|2014|p=10}} 

Hall was a research scientist at the [[Columbia University College of Physicians & Surgeons]] before joining the [[National Institutes of Health]] (NIH) in 1959.{{sfn|NIH Record|2014|p=10}} At NIH, she joined the [[National Institute of Arthritis, Metabolism and Digestive Diseases]] which later became the [[National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases]].{{sfn|Valera|2022}}{{sfn|NIH Record|2014|p=10}} 

Hall worked with [[Elizabeth F. Neufeld]] studying genetic conditions affecting [[Lysosome|lysosomes]].{{sfn|Valera|2022}} These disorders can cause skeletal abnormalities, intellectual disabilities, and a shortened lifespan. In 1982, the duo’s research earned Neufeld the [[Lasker-DeBakey Clinical Medical Research Award]].{{sfn|Valera|2022}} Hall, an African American scientist, did not receive the award, even though Neufeld did not want her colleague’s work to go unrecognized.{{sfn|Valera|2022}} Hall retired in 1999.{{sfn|Valera|2022}}

== Personal life ==
Hall was a classically trained pianist and cellist.{{sfn|Valera|2022}}{{sfn|NIH Record|2014|p=10}} In the early 1960s, she began tutoring inner-city elementary school students. Hall continued for ten years, then returned to tutoring after retiring from NIH.{{sfn|NIH Record|2014|p=10}} Hall was a tennis fan and regularly attended the [[US Open (tennis)|US Open]].{{sfn|NIH Record|2014|p=10}}

Hall had a daughter and son.{{sfn|NIH Record|2014|p=10}}

Hall died May 28, 2014, in [[Washington, D.C.]]{{sfn|NIH Record|2014|p=10}}
